body.p: S1000D® is an international specification for the procurement and production of technical publications (mainly used in aerospace and aviation industries). It is an XML-based specification for preparing, managing, and using equipment maintenance and operations information.

S1000D® has a modular architecture based on the following components:
Data Module - An XML-based, uniquely identified unit of information that can be managed, reused, and exchanged independently within the S1000D environment.
Data Module Structure - Describes the internal organization of a Data Module, typically divided into:
The Identification and Status part that identifies the Data Module within the CSDB structure.
The Content part that is the detailed information of the Data Module.
Common Source DataBase (CSDB) - The managed repository where S1000D objects (such as Data Modules, Publication Modules, and illustrations) are stored, controlled, and related to each other, and from which publications are assembled.
Business Rules Exchange (BREX) - A specialized Data Module that defines project- or organization-specific business rules governing how S1000D is applied, and against which other Data Modules can be checked for conformance.
Publication Module (PM) - An XML-based control file that defines the structure, sequence, and inclusion of Data Modules in a deliverable publication, effectively acting as the publication's table of contents.
Information Control Number (ICN) - A unique identifier assigned to illustrations and other multimedia objects, so they can be managed and referenced as standalone entities within the CSDB.
Data Dispatch Note (DDN) - A control document used to describe, package, and manage the exchange of Data Modules and related S1000D objects between organizations or systems.
Data Module Requirement List (DMRL) - A structured list of required Data Modules for a project, used as a planning and tracking tool before and during authoring.
Comment - A Data Module type used to record review comments, feedback, or annotations that reference one or more existing Data Modules.

section.title: Default Document Templates
section.p: You can get assistance with creating new S1000D® Data Modules or Publication Modules for issues 4.0, 4.1, and 4.2 by using the provided file templates available when creating new documents from templatesnew documents from templates.

section.title: Default Schema for Validation and Content Completion
section.p: The default schemas (version 4.x) used for validation and content completion are stored in /frameworks/s1000d-base/ (with separate folders for each supported issue).

S1000D document editing features include schema-guiding, validation, and content completion support. Also, documentation for S1000D elements and attributes can be viewed directly in the content completion window and in the Attributes view.

p.note: It is possible to integrate support for other S1000D versions (such as 2.x, 3.x, 5.x, 6.x). For details, see: .

section.title: Quick Fix Support
section.p: S1000D documents support some Quick Fixes. For example, a default Schematron rule verifies if the DM code is consistent with the file name in S1000D data modules and if a mismatch is detected, a Quick Fix option is available to automatically align the two.

section.title: Author Mode Actions
section.p: S1000D documents can be edited in the Author visual editing mode, while switching between full-width, or large-font styles. The following dedicated actions are available in the toolbar (and the S1000D menu) when editing S1000D documents:

dlentry.dd: Inserts a reference to a data module (DM) or project module (PM).
Inserts a reference to an image (e.g. CGM, PNG, JPG) at the cursor position. You can optionally specify values for the Title, Width, Height, or Scale attributes.
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em01" (bold).
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em04" (overline).
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em05" (strikethrough).

Surrounds the selected text with a subscript element, used for inserting a character (number, letter, or symbol) that will appear slightly below the baseline and slightly smaller than the rest of the text.

Surrounds the selected text with a superscript element, used for inserting a character (number, letter, or symbol) that will appear slightly above the baseline and slightly smaller than the rest of the text.
Inserts a list item in the current list type.
Inserts a sequential list at the cursor position. A child list item is also automatically inserted by default.
Inserts a simple random (unordered) list at the cursor position. A child list item is also automatically inserted by default.
Inserts an unordered random list at the cursor position. A child list item is also automatically inserted by default.
Inserts a definition list at the cursor position. A child list item is also automatically inserted by default.
Opens a dialog box that allows you to configure and insert a table. You can generate a header and footer, set the number of rows and columns of the table and decide how the table is framed.
Inserts a new table row with empty cells below the current row. This action is available when the cursor is positioned inside a table.
Deletes the table row located at the cursor position or multiple rows in a selection.
Inserts a new table column with empty cells after the current column. This action is available when the cursor is positioned inside a table.
Deletes the table column located at the cursor position or multiple columns in a selection.
Joins the content of the selected table cells (both horizontally and vertically).

Splits the cell at the cursor location. If detects more than one option to split the cell, a dialog box will be displayed that allows you to select the number of rows or columns to split the cell into.

section.p: The following legacy actions are available in the S1000D menu (but not on the toolbar):

dlentry.dd: Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em02" (italic).
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em03" (underline).

section.title: Floating Contextual Toolbar
section.p: Some of the most common S1000D Author mode actions are available on a dynamic floating toolbar that is triggered when you select content in supported locations within an S1000D document. The toolbar offers actions tailored to the current S1000D editing context.

section.title: BREX Editing and Transformation
section.p: BREX modules can be edited in the Text or Author mode with content completion and validation support. You can also convert BREX modules to Schematron using the provided transformation scenario.

section.title: Smart Paste
section.p: Content can be copied from web browsers or Word documents and pasted into S1000D documents while preserving structure and formatting.

section.title: Inserting References via Drag/Drop
section.p: You can drag Data Modules (DM), Publication Modules (PM), or Illustrated Content Numbers (ICN) and drop them within an S1000D document and the system will automatically generate the appropriate reference structure according to S1000D standards.

body.note: To display the CGM images that are commonly used in S1000D documents, you have to install the CGM Add-on.

section.title: Publishing
section.p: The Data Modules (DM) can be published to PDF using the S1000D Data Module PDF transformation scenario. Any images referenced in the original files are preserved in the generated output.
Data Modules can also be published as HTML files for preview (with images) and offline review in a web browser using the S1000D Data Module HTML (Preview) scenario.
